column2: 4.1. Strategic awareness

Do you have a definition of open data reuse in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify it.
column4:
The law on open data gives the following definition:
« réutilisation » : l’utilisation par des personnes physiques ou morales de documents détenus par :
a) des organismes du secteur public, à des fins commerciales ou non commerciales autres que l’objectif initial de la mission de service public pour lequel les documents ont été produits, à l’exception de l’échange de documents entre des organismes du secteur public aux seules fins de l’exercice de leur mission de service public ; ou
b) des entreprises publiques, à des fins commerciales ou non commerciales autres que l’objectif initial de fournir les services d’intérêt général pour lequel les documents ont été produits, à l’exception de l’échange de documents entre des entreprises publiques et des organismes du secteur public aux seules fins de l’exercice de leur mission de service public ;

column2:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of open data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
column4:
The use of the open data portal and of its data sets is monitored in detail, which allows to gain insights about re-use cases and their impact. In the portal, the internal statistic dashboard which renders key information about every dataset, is a good way to track the popularity of datasets, from the perspective of the data producers.
We keep an eye on the exchanges between data users and providers in the corresponding portal sections, to deduce possibly interesting re-use cases, and - as far as possible with the available means - we try to know more in order  to properly document the re-use to evaluate it's impact as well as to use it as an example to trigger further visibility for open data.
A particular case are API's where it is possible to require the use of a personal key, which obliges re-users to  be identified and the data providers to get detailed information about the uses. This is also the case of the geoportal API, which is used a lot at the national level, or the  public transport API for example.
Currently however these insights are not yet handled in a coordinated way.

The portal API allows access to datasets, and is monitored. The analytics are presented on every dataset in the back-office to all data producers, acting as an automated feedback mechanism.

For Explanation:

column4: Indeed one of the main sections of our national data portal is the re-use section, which is supposed to gather and showcase real use cases of existing open data.This section is progressing well in the last time because of our systematic endeavor to identify interesting cases and to document them. [update 16/08/2023] Any citizen or administration with an account on the open data portal can publish a reuse. Moreover, the Information and press service has organised a technological watch. This watch aggregates news coming from the luxembourgish newspapers and also online media. A daily keywords based search brings all articles related to open data. The articles are then reviewed by the open data team and published as a reuse on the open data portal if relevant.

The AEV (Administration de l'Environnement) has currently published 7 datasets on air quality on OpenData: Air Quality Datasets. We do not know if these are also actually being used for the protection of biodiversity and thus cannot provide written proof so far.
Regarding noise data, the data owners have already been in touch within the framework of a research group at the University of Salford to ensure that these data are used in the scope of projects about bird diversity.

column7:
The solar cadastre is an interesting dataset in this regard (https://data.public.lu/fr/datasets/analyse-densoleillement/) and it is used for analysis and project planning in the context of individuals as well as of collectivities, for example with the help of the geoportal functionalities (re-use of the data in the geoportal map application https://map.geoportail.lu/theme/energie?version=3&zoom=16&X=696269&Y=6379269&lang=en&rotation=0&layers=1818-1813-2537&opacities=1-1-1&time=----&bgLayer=basemap_2015_global) or other more specific re-uses. In the same context, the city of Luxembourg proposes online applications of this and correlated data (https://www.vdl.lu/fr/la-ville/engagements-de-la-ville/actions-environnementales/subventions-attribuables-en-vue-de-la-protection-du-climat/installations-pour-energies-renouvelables#cadastre-solaire), like the estimation of possible subsidies. Another interesting project is about an analysis on dangerous and inadequate pedestrian crossings https://data.public.lu/fr/organizations/zentrum-fir-urban-gerechtegkeet/, based on a re-use of open data.
Some other, new, re-uses show a growing impact of open data in the context of more environment-friendly cities :
https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/energieauer-key-energy-figures-for-luxembourg/ with a dashboard provided by the national climate agency,
https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/whispers-of-the-wheel/ Whispers of the wheel, a dashboard about the availability of rental bikes in the city of Luxembourg
https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/air-quality-luxembourg/ , a dashboard about the air quality in Luxembourg

1.	We consider that the following study has an impact on prevention: Climate and Energy: The Climate-Ecology Situation in Luxembourg (https://data.public.lu/fr/datasets/climate-and-energy-the-climate-ecology-situation-in-luxembourg/)
Based on this study, the municipality of Esch, for example, conducted a more detailed analysis of their terrain. Additionally, the LIST (Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology) has started a larger-scale and more detailed analysis.
2.	From the national emission inventories, the following datasets are currently available on OpenData: Air Quality: https://data.public.lu/fr/datasets/air-quality-spatial-emissions-mapping-of-luxembourg/ and https://data.public.lu/fr/datasets/climate-and-energy-national-emission-inventories/
More explanations can be found on emwelt.lu: Climate and Energy - Emission Inventory (https://environnement.public.lu/fr/klima-an-energie/changement-climatique/inventaire-ges0.html)
These data also flow into the PNEC (National Energy and Climate Plan), where most of the measures are recorded: National Energy and Climate Plan Update (https://environnement.public.lu/content/dam/environnement/actualites/2023/juillet-2023/pnec/pnec-projet-de-mise-jour-luxembourg.pdf)
Due to the obligation of fulfilling the HVD regulation, further publications will have to be made on the nation OpenData portal.

column7:
We have been able to detect and document reuses on this topic:
- https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/tableaux-interactifs-sur-les-demandeurs-demploi-inscrits-a-ladem/ These are dashboards about unemployment in Luxembourg with lots of details, and the evolution of some data is also available. They have been developed by the public sector. They show that the category "IT systems and telecommunication" is one of the most important categories in terms of job offers. This information helped the Education ministry to develop a new concept of professional training in this domain, with the initiative DLH (digital learning hub) which started in 2022. The goal of DLH is to assist persons in  their professional transition to software development and other IT skills. It has been a great success, and an additional training institue  "42Luxembourg" has been created https://42luxembourg.lu/ which is an example of PPP.
- https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/unemployment-luxembourg-facilitons-lemploi-chiffres-cles/ this dashboard is quite similar but maybe more synthetic and has been developed by a private sector company.
Both reuses are based on the same datasets.
